target_customer: Pharma and biotech partners and Talus itself as a drug developer pursuing transcription factor and other regulome targets
problem: Many gene regulator proteins (the regulome) are hard to drug because they fail to function in artificial biochemical assays, so drug screening on them rarely works.
business_model: Platform-based drug discovery: internal pipeline plus partnerships and collaborations
product_category: Biotech drug discovery platform (proteomics, automation, AI)

founders.name: Alex Federation
education: Trained at Harvard under Jay Bradner in medicinal chemistry and drug screening for gene regulators, then in genome sciences at the University of Washington (per YC page and Eqvista interview); degree not stated
founders.background_notes: Eqvista interview says his Harvard work contributed to several therapeutic programs and startups.

founders.name: Lindsay Pino
education: Trained at the Broad Institute, the University of Washington and the University of Pennsylvania (per YC page); degrees not stated

competitors.name: Foghorn Therapeutics
competitors.what: Chromatin regulation platform targeting gene regulation machinery for cancer, with a transcription factor deal with Merck
competitors.traction_then: Listed on Nasdaq in October 2020 and signed a Merck collaboration targeting a single transcription factor

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining automated live-cell processing, next-gen proteomics and analytics to measure drug effects across the whole regulome in one experiment is research-grade work needing wet lab automation.

defensibility.rationale: Platform data and proteomics know-how are hard to copy, but biotech outcomes depend on clinical results that were years away at founding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge as of 2025; Talus signed a collaboration with PRISM BioLab in December 2025.

market_need_then: Gene regulators and transcription factors were widely described as hard-to-drug targets, and Foghorn's 2020 IPO and Merck deal showed investor and pharma appetite for the area.

branding.domain_note: Uses talus.bio; no acquisition story found.

identity.visual_style: Minimal and technical, large plain headings and numbered sections
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and scientific, tagline 'Let's work on the hard targets'

branding.brand_signature: Ptarmigan, the name of its flagship model

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is functional and scientific, with no press or community evidence about the brand itself; it neither helped nor hurt a science-led, investor-led business.

outcome_analysis: Talus is still active and has funded itself with a 2022 raise, a 2023 grant and an 2024 seed-plus round led by Two Bear Capital, then signed a pharma-style tools collaboration in December 2025. Its founders have deep regulome and proteomics training, which fits the platform. No clinical outcome is reported yet, so the story is early and unproven.
notes: The GeekWire 2022 and 2023 articles were seen as headlines on the YC page and in search results (pages returned 403), so amounts for those two come from headlines; the 2022 round stage and investors are not stated in what I saw. The 2024 round was confirmed by Business Wire and Fierce Biotech listings and the Eqvista interview. Aggregator totals ($19.6M, $24.7M) conflict and are not used. Founding year is 2020 per YC page; some aggregators say 2019. Search results mention a 2021 YC cohort conflict (W21 vs S21); the directory says Summer 2021.
